faq.subtitle: How Writ works, who it is for, and how your data is protected.

q1.a: Writ is a CRM for political campaigns in Canada. It brings your contacts, lists, email, social media messages and volunteers into one place, in English and French.

q2.a: Candidates, riding associations and advocacy groups of any size, at any level of government. Writ is non-partisan and works with campaigns across the political spectrum.

q3.a: In Canadian data centres. Your data does not leave Canada.

q4.q: Can other campaigns see our data?
q4.a: No. Each campaign's data is separated in the database itself, and every request is checked against your team's membership. Another campaign cannot reach your data, even by mistake.

q5.a: Yes. Every screen, email template and form is available in English and French, and each of your contacts can be reached in the language they prefer.

q6.q: Do you sell or share voter data?
q6.a: Never. Your supporters' data belongs to your campaign. We do not sell it, share it or use it for anything else.

q7.a: We are opening a pilot for a small number of campaigns. Book a demo and we will be in touch.

footer.n1: Writ is non-partisan software. It offers the same service to campaigns across the political spectrum and does not endorse, support or oppose any candidate, party, position or referendum outcome.
footer.n2: Supporter data is stored in Canadian data centres and is encrypted in transit and at rest. It is not transferred outside Canada for storage or processing.
footer.n3: Each campaign owns the data it puts into Writ. Writ processes that data only to provide the service to that campaign, and never sells it, shares it with another campaign or uses it for any other purpose, including training AI models.
footer.n4: Each campaign's data is separated from every other campaign's in the database itself, and every request is checked against the campaign's own team. Access within a campaign follows the roles its owners and admins assign.
footer.n5: Writ is in development. Features described on this page may not all be available during the pilot. Availability, pricing and terms are confirmed with each campaign when it joins.
footer.n6: Writ is not affiliated with Elections Canada, with any provincial, territorial or municipal elections authority, or with any political party. Lists of electors supplied by an elections authority remain subject to that authority's rules on their use.
footer.n7: Each campaign remains responsible for complying with the election, election finance, privacy and anti-spam laws that apply to it, including Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation (CASL). Writ provides tools to record consent and handle unsubscribes, but does not give legal advice.
footer.n8: Email is delivered through Amazon Web Services in Canada. Facebook and Instagram features use Meta's platforms, require each campaign to connect its own accounts, and are subject to Meta's terms.
footer.n9: Every team member signs in with multi-factor authentication. Exports, role changes, sends and other sensitive actions are recorded in a log that cannot be edited or deleted.
footer.n10: Facebook and Instagram are trademarks of Meta Platforms, Inc.; Writ is not affiliated with or endorsed by Meta. Names, places and figures in product images are fictional. For more information, see the <terms>Terms of service</terms> and the <privacy>Privacy policy</privacy>.
footer.closingLine: Built in Canada, for the people who show up.

Manifesto.metaDescription: Why we are building Writ: reaching people around a cause, without the extra work.

entry.meaning: The order that starts an election.
entry.reveal: And the place to run what comes next.

p1.title: It is time to rethink how campaigns reach people.
p1.s1: Newsletters and door knocks. Phone calls and town halls. Facebook messages, emails to the office, a note on the back of a petition.
p1.s2: People reach out in more ways than ever, and every message deserves an answer. The work behind each one never stops.
p1.s3: For years, campaigns and offices have faced the same choice: stay small, or drown in software built for someone else.
p1.s4: Every new channel meant another login, another spreadsheet and another tool only one volunteer understood.
p1.s5: We were told that is just how organizing works.

p2.title: Times have changed.
p2.s1: The tools campaigns were given were built for marketers and sales teams, full of funnels, pipelines and settings nobody asked for.
p2.s2: The people doing this work deserve tools that are clear the first time they open them, whatever their age or experience.
p2.s3: They deserve software that does the busywork, so they can spend their time with people.

p3.title: What does organizing without the extra work mean?
p3.s1: It means every supporter, conversation and case in one place, kept in Canada.
p3.s2: It means mailings, messages and follow-ups that send themselves, and results you can read at a glance.
p3.s3: It means rejecting the idea that reaching more people must mean more work.

b1.because: Because the people doing this work have better things to learn than menus.

b2.because: Because no message, call or case should be left waiting.

b3.because: Because supporter lists are never sold, shared or mixed with anyone else’s.

b4.because: Because you should see that it is working, not how the machinery works.

close.title: This is organizing without the extra work.
close.s1: That is why we are here. That is what we are building:
close.s2: One simple place to stay in touch with the people you serve, built in Canada.
